The test image shows split soybean stems/roots with:
- Pale/bleached internal pith tissue
- Dark black granular material inside the stem cavity (sclerotia)
- Root/lower stem region affected

This strongly suggests **Charcoal Rot** (Macrophomina phaseolina) — the hallmark tiny black microsclerotia inside bleached stem pith. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference image confirms it: tiny black microsclerotia scattered throughout pale/bleached internal stem tissue — exactly what's visible in the test image. The dark granular mass in the split stems of the test image is the classic sign of Charcoal Rot.
